findings.windowsClientBehavior: The current Microsoft passkey page says Windows 11 version 24H2 prompts for per-application passkey privacy consent. Users can change individual application access in Settings; declining consent prevents registration and authentication for that application.
findings.enterprisePolicyTarget: The same page still says enterprise consent policies are currently available in Windows Insider builds and were targeted for general availability by the end of June 2026.
findings.publishedPolicyCsp: The current Privacy Policy CSP continues to mark LetAppsAccessPasskeys, its ForceAllowTheseApps, ForceDenyTheseApps and UserInControlOfTheseApps lists, and LetAppsAccessPasskeysEnumeration as Windows Insider Preview. These nodes are device-scoped; per-app lists accept Microsoft Store Package Family Names.
findings.reconciliation: The published general-availability target date has passed, but the current Microsoft policy page still describes the controls as Insider Preview. This review does not establish released-target support or behavior.

decision.implementation: Keep the enterprise-policy candidate deferred. Do not infer stable registry/CSP support from the date target, host ADMX presence or the Windows 11 per-app consent UI. Preserve per-application user choice; do not substitute a global Boolean or default-deny policy.
nextEvidenceNeeded: Microsoft publishes stable applicability for the base and per-app policy nodes on a named released Windows target.
Target acceptance establishes observed state, apply behavior, user-choice preservation and exact saved-state restore on that supported target.

partial: Current primary-source review reconfirms the policy-support discrepancy and records the current user-visible per-app consent behavior.
deferred: Enterprise-managed per-app passkey consent remains deferred pending published stable-target applicability and exact reversible policy semantics.

estimates.adjustment: None; this new Windows-control review closes no legacy outcome.
